title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 354
paragraphs: The final deliverance from the Ethiopian came about, they said, as follows. He fled away because he had seen a vision in his sleep, in which it seemed to him that a man came and stood beside him and advised him to gather together all the priests of Egypt and cut them in half through the middle. Having seen this dream, he said it seemed to him that the gods were showing this to him in order to give him a pretext — so that he might commit an impious act against religion and thus receive some punishment either from the gods or from men. He would not, however, do so. In truth, he said, the time had expired during which it had been prophesied that he would rule Egypt before departing from it. For while he was still in Ethiopia, the oracles the Ethiopians consult had told him it was fated that he should rule Egypt for fifty years. Since this time was now running out, and the vision of the dream also disturbed him, Sabacos departed from Egypt of his own accord.
